scope: Representative new construction in 1976–1985, retained by both renovation states. It is a nominal period model with declared normal-use defaults, not a verified individual building. Material grades and source records remain unchanged.

tabula.source_meaning: Original envelope references are BETSI stock means with no complete layer recipe. The brochure illustrates an AAC wall without specifying a thickness or grade; this catalogue uses an independently period-supported timber variant. 1978 is an EPSM representative year within the source era, not a TABULA construction date.

wall.source_supported_family: From 1965: main vertical timber framing plus an insulated horizontal inner cross-frame, external wind sheathing, internal board/gypsum and vapour control. The drawing specifies a four-inch main frame and a two-inch cross-member; it does not establish the retained 145 mm main-frame depth.
wall.nominal_choice: Retain the existing 145 mm late-period main frame and 13 mm gypsum. Reuse the accepted 50 mm nominal inner cross-frame and 12 mm porous wood-fibre windboard. The existing 15% whole-wall framing allowance and all material thermal properties are unchanged.

period_plausibility.scope: Approximate independent era mean, not a layer prescription or acceptance target.

wall.renovation: Reuse shared 22 mm timber panel plus 45/70 mm facade-wool additions outside all retained original nominal core layers. TABULA prescribes the added thickness and panelled finish; grade and panel depth are explicit EPSM defaults.
wall.remaining_limits: Original cladding, battens and ventilation cavity remain unquantified project details. Thin air/vapour controls, fasteners, interfaces and moisture design are project requirements. The generic windboard thermal grade does not establish asphalt content or full weather performance; its retained-stock carbon factors remain unknown.

period_source_locators.tabula: TABULA.xlsm#'Tab.Building'!BD811,BN811,CJ811; 'Tab.Building.Constr'!I311:R311,AC311. The roof code is SE.Ceiling.ReEx.03.01, a synthetic BETSI average for 1976–1985, not a physical layer recipe. Tab.Building!V811 is blank; 1978 is an EPSM representative year.

period_context.locator: Energimyndigheten ET2009:19, printed p.11 / PDF index10, right-hand table: 1976–1985 original attic mean U0.18. The separate 1955-onwards drawing gives 100–180mm mineral wool and c/c1200, not a post-1975 depth prescription. Example U-values use an older calculation convention.

period_arrangement.locator: Bjerking R106:1978, printed p.43 / PDF index43, Figure2234 (1965 onwards): mineral-wool boards between joists, continuous mineral-wool mat above, underpanel and gypsum/wood-fibre lining. The drawing states c/c600 and joists up to3x9 inches; it does not specify the mat depths selected here.

declared_defaults.selection: Representative 1978 ceiling: retain the former nominal200mm framed depth and existing mineral-wool grade; add50mm continuous original wool following the documented over-joist arrangement. The total250mm is an explicit EPSM completion default, not a layer recipe recovered from TABULA or the ET2009:19 100–180mm illustration. The ET1976–1985 meanU0.18 is broad period-performance context, not a target used to solve a layer depth.
declared_defaults.geometry: Nominal75mm joist width at 1200 mm centres gives6.25% timber, reusing the declared regular-framing family selected for SFSE02. Width, spacing and50mm continuous depth are engineering defaults for this representative ceiling. The period detail supporting the over-joist arrangement uses c/c600, so its framing dimensions are not claimed as the adopted recipe. Joist sizing, supports, spans, connectors and structural verification remain project details.
declared_defaults.materials: Historic wool conductivity0.04W/(mK), density29kg/m³ and specific heat1030J/(kgK), and the shared softwood and lining properties are unchanged. The renovation states retain all original layers and add the accepted 200/500 mm loose wool at conductivity0.037W/(mK). Thin air/vapour control and wind protection, ventilation and moisture design remain project details; this nominal model does not certify code compliance.

attic.nominal_recipe: Retain the existing 200 mm main ceiling depth but use a 75 mm joist-width default at 1200 mm centres (6.25% timber), with 50 mm continuous mineral wool above it. Retain 22 mm timber underboard and 13 mm gypsum. Total nominal original wool depth 250 mm.
attic.source_scope: The period source supports insulation between framing plus a continuous mat above. Exact 200+50 mm depths and 75/c1200 framing are declared engineering defaults, not recovered TABULA dimensions. Earlier 100–180 mm examples are not treated as the 1976–85 depth prescription.
attic.renovation: Retain the original ceiling and reuse accepted 200/500 mm loose-wool additions. The existing matching Supafil EPD reference remains; its retained source capture is in evidence/sf_se02_source_review.json#/carbon_review/loft_epd.

source.u_basis: BETSI area-weighted stock average including soil heat transfer under ISO 13370:2007(E), not material-only resistance; the underlying statistic includes at-grade slabs and basement ground floors.
betsi_locators: BETSI Energi i bebyggelsen (2010), printed p.17, U-value calculation assumptions
BETSI Energi i bebyggelsen (2010), printed pp.19–20, slab/basement-floor population and geometry assumptions
BETSI Energi i bebyggelsen (2010), printed p.166, Appendix 2, Table 8, SF 1976–1985
source.placement_scope: Brochure illustration places added insulation above the existing slab. It does not prescribe the EPSM concrete finish, its exact thickness or a complete moisture-safe floor system.
source.source_recipe_scope: TABULA supplies a synthetic BETSI average and no original material recipe; Tab.Building.Constr!AC301 explicitly records that limitation.

floor.baseline: Retain the user P04 nominal 70 mm under-slab EPS and 120 mm concrete; replace the 10 mm timber finish with a 40 mm bonded mineral cement finish. All depths and finish choice are explicit representative defaults.
floor.chronology_scope: Modin and Sundberg (2012), EPS i grund, printed p.6 (PDF page 16), reports compressed mineral-wool under-slab boards as dominant in the 1970s with occasional EPS/XPS substitution. EPS below a 1978 slab is plausible but not asserted to be the majority practice. The 70 mm depth is the retained user P04 default. TABULA has no exact building year (Tab.Building!V811 blank); 1978 is a declared representative year within 1976–1985.
floor.renovation: Reuse warm-side 40/45 mm EPS at lambda 0.036 plus 50 mm floating mineral cement finish. Retain all original layers; floor rise 90/95 mm.
floor.finish_scope: Shared Generic HW Concrete is a thermal/concrete-family carbon proxy, not an exact proprietary screed. Reinforcement, load distribution, moisture, separation and clearances remain project inputs.
floor.boundary: Soil-facing slab on ground. Source effective ground U includes soil heat transfer and stock geometry; nominal material-layer U cannot be accepted directly against it. Project geometry, soil and ground method remain unresolved inputs.

advanced.selection: Reuse the accepted shared TABULA advanced replacement.

window_scope: Original glazing g 0.70 and frame fraction 0.30 give whole-aperture SHGC 0.49; glazing VT 0.75 is an EPSM default giving aperture VT 0.525. Renovation optics follow source g and the same frame convention. Boverket window IDs remain declared modern family proxies.
verification: Organized independent cases/sf_se03.json controls source values and declared geometry. Fixed TABULA benchmark tables and 20% tolerance remain unchanged; all physical checks calculate forward. Shared-definition guards retain school SE03 assignments and thermal properties. Unknown carbon modules and project inputs remain visible.
